myosin light-chain kinase is expressed in neural cells.

myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK), the enzyme responsible for phosphorylating myosin, is present in neurons and glial cells, and that this protein is localized to the cytoplasm and cytoskeleton of astrocytes, and to the cytoploplasm, cytoskeleton, and processes of cerebellar granular neurons.
myosin light-chain kinase, the enzyme responsible for myosin lightchain phosphorylation, is found in neurons and glial cells.

understanding the molecular basis for the control of cell movement.
the identification of proteins that are associated with the cytoplasm of cultured astrocytes.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal and glial motility and the role of myosin light-chain kinase in the regulation of this process.

the MLCK immunoreactive proteins are not identical to the myosin light chains.
MLCK is present in both neurons and glial cells, that it is associated with both cytoplasmic and membrane-bound structures, and that its presence may be related to the motile functions of the cell.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+/CaM-activated enzyme myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK), which phosphorylates the light-chain subunit of nonmuscle myosin, is widely distributed in neurons and glial cells.
myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK), the enzyme that catalyzes myosin lightchain phosphorylation, is expressed in both neurons and glial cells.

the myosin light chains of non-muscle myosin are phosphorylated in neurons, astrocytes and other glial cells, and that the myosinal phosphorylation reaction is catalysed by the same Ca2+/calmodyulin-activated myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK; EC 2.7.11.17) that regulates smooth muscle contraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MLCK is present in neural cells and may be involved in motility-related functions.
MLCK is expressed in neurons as well as in glia and is present in both cytosol and cytoskeleton.
myosin light-chain kinase, which is a protein that is important in muscle contraction, is also expressed in neurons and in astrocytes.
